steps.title: Create & fund
steps.headline:
Talk is cheap.
Back your promise.
steps.description: Choose your role, payment and both deposits. The creator first funds the amount required for their own role.
steps.meme: A little less talk. A real commitment.
steps.note: Agree on trade details off-chain. The contract does not store the agreement text.

steps.title: The other side accepts
steps.headline:
You're in?
Then I'm in.
steps.description: Share the order link. The other participant reviews the terms and funds the amount for the opposite role.
steps.meme: Now we're both taking this seriously.
steps.note: The payer funds the payment plus their deposit. The payee funds their own deposit.

steps.title: Activate the promise
steps.headline:
The right person.
A shared commitment.
steps.description: For public orders, the creator approves the accepting participant. Designated orders activate as soon as the named participant accepts.
steps.meme: Check your counterparty. Then say yes.
steps.note: After a public order is accepted, either party can still cancel before activation. Once active, there is no cancellation or timeout refund.

steps.title: Deliver & confirm
steps.headline:
Don't look at me.
We both say yes.
steps.description: Complete delivery and acceptance off-chain. Each participant then confirms completion. A confirmation cannot be undone.
steps.meme: Finish the agreement before you confirm.
steps.note: One confirmation alone does not release the funds.

steps.title: Automatic settlement
steps.headline:
Two yeses.
One settled deal.
steps.description: The second completion confirmation settles the order in the same transaction. No extra settlement transaction is needed.
steps.meme: Both agree. The numbers are settled.
steps.note: Settlement creates claimable amounts. It does not transfer funds back automatically.

steps.title: Claim your share
steps.headline:
Your share. My share.
Good doing business.
steps.description: The payer claims their deposit. The payee claims the payment and their deposit. Each party claims independently and can choose a recipient.
steps.meme: A promise kept. See you next time.
steps.note: A failed claim does not block the other participant. Change the recipient and retry if needed.

boundaries: Cancel before activation, according to your role
Claim separately after cancellation or settlement

questions.q: Will clearing the browser cache delete my orders?
questions.a: No. Orders live on the blockchain. The cache only stores this browser's index and sync progress. Sync again to rebuild it; the first scan may take longer.

questions.q: Why does ERC20 require approval first?
questions.a: The token contract requires you to authorize Pact Lock to collect the amount due. Approval and order creation or acceptance are separate transactions. Gas is paid in the native currency.

questions.q: Will funds be refunded if the other side never confirms?
questions.a: No. Active orders have no cancellation, timeout refund, arbitration or administrator release. Agree on the details off-chain and check the participant and amounts before activation.

questions.q: Why must I claim after settlement?
questions.a: Settlement determines each participant's allocation. Claims are separate, so a failed transfer to one party does not block the other.
Agree on the trade details off-chain. The contract stores roles, asset, amounts, participant addresses and state. It does not store agreement text, hashes or links.

shortSteps: The creator funds their own role.
The other party funds the opposite role.
Public orders need creator approval; designated orders activate on acceptance.
Deliver off-chain, then each party confirms.
Claim independently, with a recipient of your choice.
